risks: Resource registry search catches provider errors and returns empty contributions, so using it as the only relation API would conceal denied/offline/missingDependency failures.
ResourceItem.id/title/data are generic resource presentation, not proof of authorized canonical EntityRef; title collision or nativeId-only joins can link the wrong private entity.
authorizeRox2Action and ProjectVisibility predicates trust supplied grants/visibility; treating them as authoritative resolvers bypasses authenticated per-entity/field policy and revoke checks.
registerExternalBinding protects provider/account/type/remoteId namespaces, not the full personal sourceStoreId/ownerPrincipalId/nativeId contract; accepted LSX-WP-002 remains necessary.
Generic custom relations must not be encoded as blocks/assigned/member-of just to reuse an existing enum; native parent/project semantics and cycle/deletion policies differ.
Forward/inverse endpoints may live in separate authorities. A cloned in-memory membership result or local queued receipt is not a recoverable durable inverse commit.
Tombstone refs and unknown/denied/ambiguous import mappings must remain unresolved, not disappear or reconnect by equal title; repeated imports must not duplicate inverse edges.
Concurrent cardinality/schema/row changes require atomic preconditions and idempotent recovery; blind journal replay can overwrite current writes or bypass revoked grants.

The only approved shared patch is registry.ts. API dispatch, UI mounting, event consumer and ten locale updates require reviewed scope or existing accepted extension hooks; writing only the four new files cannot meet end-to-end DoD.
